title: UKPNP Holds Historic Event on 28 April 1949 Karachi Agreement with Great Turnout and Mass Mobilisation in Rawalakot, Poonch.
excerpt: A comprehensive press release detailing the UKPNP's landmark Rawalakot event commemorating the Karachi Agreement, featuring leadership addresses, public participation, and calls for peaceful dialogue.
author: Special Correspondent --- The Mirror Jammu Kashmir

heroImage.caption: UKPNP Public Gathering on the Occasion of Event on the Karachi Agreement, 28th April 2026 Rawalakot Poonch

body.text: RAWALAKOT: UKPNP HISTORIC EVENT ON THE 28 APRIL 1949 KARACHI AGREEMENT

Rawalakot, Poonch, 28 April 2026 --- The United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) organised a historic and highly attended public gathering in Rawalakot, Poonch, to mark the anniversary of the 28 April 1949 Karachi Agreement. The event drew a remarkable turnout, with central leadership, women, youth, and supporters from across the region participating in large numbers.

body.caption: UKPNP leadership addressing the Rawalakot gathering

body.text: The programme, held at Akbar Hotel Rawalakot and followed by a rally through the city, reflected the party's long-standing commitment to peaceful struggle, democratic rights, and the reunification of the State of Jammu and Kashmir. Participants raised powerful slogans including 'We want freedom,' 'We want a united independent State of Jammu and Kashmir,' 'No to forced division,' 'Aar paar joor do, Kashmir hamara chhor do,' 'Long Live UKPNP,' and 'Long Live United Independent State of Jammu and Kashmir.' The venue was decorated with UKPNP flags, historical flags of the State of Jammu and Kashmir, and banners representing the party's vision and political struggle.
UKPNP Calls for Continued Dialogue to Secure a Peaceful and Democratic Resolution of Issues in Azad Jammu and Kashmir

The programme was chaired by Madam Sardar Tania Khan, Senior Vice Chairperson UKPNP, with Sardar Riaz Khan, President UKPNP Canada, serving as the chief guest, and Advocate Sardar Rashid Yousaf, President UKPNP North America, attending as the special guest.

body.caption: Delegates and participants during the rally

body.text: The organisational leadership of the event was carried out by Sardar Atif Khan, President UKPNP District Poonch; Fazil Jammu Kashmiri, General Secretary District Poonch; and Iftikhar Ahmad, Deputy Secretary Europe Zone, whose efforts ensured the successful execution of the programme. The proceedings were conducted by Fazal Jammu Kashmiri, while the reception of incoming rallies was led by Sardar Atif Khan.
"Dialogue remains the only peaceful, responsible, and effective means of resolving the issues confronting the people of Azad Jammu and Kashmir." --- Chairman Shaukat Ali Kashmiri
CHAIRMAN SHAUKAT ALI KASHMIRI'S ADDRESS

Addressing the gathering via video link, Chairman Shaukat Ali Kashmiri highlighted the historical significance of the Karachi Agreement and its consequences for the people of Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan. He stated that the agreement curtailed the powers of both regions while simultaneously acknowledging Gilgit-Baltistan as a historical part of the disputed State of Jammu and Kashmir, a fact he stressed must never be overlooked.

body.caption: Chairman Shaukat Ali Kashmiri addressing via video link

body.text: He paid tribute to Nasir Sharif, noting that although he was not present at the event, he played a key role in organising and strengthening the party in Rawalakot and remains a dedicated comrade of UKPNP. Chairman Shaukat Ali Kashmiri also praised Advocate Sardar Rashid Yousaf for his contributions to the successful organisation of the programme and congratulated Sardar Atif Khan, Fazil Jammu Kashmiri, and Iftikhar Ahmad for their tireless efforts, calling such committed comrades a true asset to the party.

He further expressed gratitude to members of the central cabinet and party workers who travelled from different regions to participate. In his address, Chairman Shaukat Ali Kashmiri also emphasised the importance of continued dialogue as the only peaceful, responsible, and effective means of resolving the political, economic, and governance-related issues confronting the people of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
"Walking away from dialogue at this stage would be counterproductive and harmful to the broader public interest."

Referring to the ongoing movement led by the Joint Awami Action Committee, he stated that the struggle has remained peaceful, legitimate, and rooted in the genuine grievances of the local population. He warned that abandoning dialogue would risk instability and undermine the legitimate demands of the people.

body.caption: UKPNP flags and banners at Akbar Hotel Rawalakot

body.text: He called for the immediate resumption of talks and urged the authorities to issue formal notifications on matters where consensus has already been achieved so that the people may begin to benefit without further delay. UKPNP leaders unanimously endorsed the continuation of dialogue until all outstanding issues are resolved, cautioning that no action should be taken that risks disorder, instability, or provides any justification for the use of force against peaceful civilians.
PARTICIPATION FROM ACROSS THE REGION

Participants attended from Mang, Sudhnuti, Thorar, Kotli, Bagh, Muzaffarabad, and various areas of District Poonch. Notable attendees included Sardar Arshad, Owais Khan, Haji Sabir Hussain from Jandala, the Chaudhry brothers from Paniola Bazaar, and representatives from multiple regions.

body.caption: Participants from across Azad Kashmir and Punjab Zone

body.text: From the Punjab Zone, participants included Sadia Khurshid, Adeeba Abbasi, Sardar Huma Khan, and Sardar Zoya Khan. UKNSO Central Vice President Israr Ahmad also attended, along with Abdul Qadeer, Member Press Club Ghazi Millat, Sardar Rashid, Sardar Liaquat, Sardar Nadeem Iqbal, Sardar Jameel Kashmiri, Kashif Siddique, Sardar Sajid, Shaukat, and many others from Rawalakot. The large turnout reflected strong public support and engagement.

body.caption: Women and youth participation at the event

body.text: SPEAKERS REAFFIRM COMMITMENT TO PEACEFUL STRUGGLE

Prominent speakers at the event included Sardar Ishtiaq Hussain, Secretary General UKPNP; Raja Muhammad Azam, Deputy Secretary General; Syeda Nighat Gardezi, Secretary Women Affairs; Syed Waqar Kazimi, senior leader and Central Committee member; Amjad Gardezi, President AJK Zone; Saad Rajput of KNSO; Mirza Aleem Shafiq Jaral; Mufti Umar Farooq; Saeed Shah of JKLF; Mushtaq Khan, President UKPNP District Sudhnuti; Kamran Khalid; Raja Faiz from Arja Bagh; and others.
"UKPNP remains committed to a peaceful, democratic, and rights-based struggle for the reunification and independence of the State of Jammu and Kashmir."

Speakers reaffirmed that UKPNP remains committed to a peaceful, democratic, and rights-based struggle for the reunification and independence of the State of Jammu and Kashmir, rooted in non-violence, political awareness, and international advocacy.
STATE SUBJECT RULE AND LEGAL CONCERNS

The UKPNP leadership expressed serious concern over ongoing violations of the State Subject Rule of 1927, stating that such violations undermine the legal and political rights of the people of the State. They demanded the immediate cancellation of all forged and fake State Subject certificates and called for urgent action to protect the lawful status and rights of genuine State Subject holders.

body.caption: Public concerns raised regarding State Subject Rule violations

body.text: The party reiterated that no red line should be crossed: no violence, no division of Jammu and Kashmir, no accession of any kind, and no actions that escalate tensions or invite repression. They stressed that contentious political and constitutional matters require sensitivity, wisdom, and sustained dialogue, while areas of agreement should be implemented without delay to build trust and confidence.
"No violence, no division, no accession --- only dialogue, unity, and protection of rights."
UKPNP reaffirmed its principled position that the people of Jammu and Kashmir must have the final and decisive say in determining their political future.
CULTURAL AND POETIC TRIBUTE
Renowned Pahari poet Hameed Kamran enriched the gathering with his poetry, paying tribute to Madam Nahla Khan and recalling the struggle of Arif Shaheed, creating emotional moments for the audience.
A significant number of youth joined UKPNP on this occasion, and Advocate Sardar Rashid Yousaf administered the oath to the newly joined members.
TRIBUTES TO INTERNATIONAL LEADERSHIP

Chairman UKPNP Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri also paid tribute to leaders abroad, including Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan, Jamil Maqsood, Sardar Rashid Yousaf, Sardar Tariq Khan, Raja Sarfraz, Qayyum Khan, Sardar Amjad Yousaf, Tahir Aziz, Sajid Hussain, Mahmood Kashmiri, Asif Abbas, Tika Khan Tahir, Aqeel Ahmed, Naveed Khan, Muhammad Riaz Khan, Sajjad Hussain, and others, acknowledging their effective role at the international level.

body.caption: UKPNP leadership honoured for international advocacy

body.text: CLOSING CEREMONY AND MEDIA COVERAGE
The event concluded with a dinner in honour of the participants, followed by closing remarks and thanks delivered by Sardar Atif Khan.
The programme was broadcast on social media platforms by Poonch TV, JK TV, Thorar Press Club, and KTV, ensuring wide public reach and engagement.
